Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### Quick answer Yes – the **MapLibre style-spec validator** can be run from the command line: ```bash # 1️⃣ Install the validator (dev-dependency is fine) npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec # 2️⃣ Run it against your exported JSON npx gl-style-validate path/to/your-style.json ``` If the file is valid you’ll see something like: ``` ✔ style.json is a valid MapLibre style (0 errors, 0 warnings) ``` If there are problems the CLI prints each error/warning with a line number and a short description, e.g.: ``` ✖ 12:5 source “my-tiles” has an unsupported “url” scheme “mapbox://” ✖ 45:12 property “glyphs” must be a URL string ``` You can then edit the JSON (or the source that generated it) until the validator reports **0 errors** (warnings can be ignored if you understand them). --- ## Why you need the validator * **Mapbox-only URLs** – `mapbox://`, `mapbox://sprites/…`, `mapbox://fonts/…` are not understood by MapLibre. * **Source-layer names** – Tile providers often use different layer names (`road` → `road_main`, etc.). * **Style-spec version** – MapLibre follows the **MapLibre Style Specification** (a superset of the Mapbox spec up to v8). The validator checks that every property you use is supported. * **Glyphs & sprites** – It ensures `glyphs` and `sprite` URLs point to reachable resources and that the font names you reference exist. Running the validator before you ship saves you from the “blank map / 401 / missing fonts” errors that are the most common post-migration surprises. --- ## Step-by-step migration checklist (including the validator) | Step | What to do | CLI / Tool | |------|------------|------------| | **1** | Replace `mapbox-gl` with `maplibre-gl` (npm install, import changes). | – | | **2** | Rename all `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` (including CSS class prefixes). | – | | **3** | **Remove the access token** and point `style` at a non-Mapbox URL. | – | | **4** | **Validate the style JSON** (see above). | `npx gl-style-validate …` | | **5** | If the validator flags `url` fields that still start with `mapbox://`, replace them with URLs that belong to your new tile source (e.g. OpenStreetMap-based vector tiles, PMTiles, MapTiler, etc.). | – | | **6** | Check `glyphs` and `sprite` URLs – they must be reachable HTTP(S) URLs. | – | | **7** | Run the map in a browser; open the console and look for any remaining “source-layer not found” or “missing font” messages. | – | | **8** | Replace any Mapbox-only APIs (`setFog`, `getFreeCameraOptions`, etc.) with their MapLibre equivalents. | – | | **9** | Swap Mapbox plugins (geocoder, directions, compare) for the MapLibre forks or open-source alternatives. | – | | **10**| Deploy once the validator reports **0 errors** and the map loads locally. | – | --- ## Tips for a smooth validation run | Situation | What to do | |-----------|------------| | **Large style files** ( > 1 MB) cause the CLI to be slow | Add `--max-old-space-size=4096` to the node command: `node --max-old-space-size=4096 ./node_modules/.bin/gl-style-validate …` | | **You get “unknown property” warnings** | Most are harmless (e.g., `metadata` fields that MapLibre ignores). If you want a clean build, remove them or move them under `metadata` where they belong. | | **You need to validate many styles** | Add a script to `package.json`:
`"validate:styles": "gl-style-validate ./styles/*.json"` | | **You want a human-readable report** | Pipe the output to a file: `npx gl-style-validate style.json > validation-report.txt` | | **You prefer a GUI** | Open the JSON in **Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io/). It will refuse to load a style that fails the spec, and it highlights the offending fields. | --- ## What the validator **doesn’t** check | Not covered | Why it’s still important | |-------------|--------------------------| | **Tile-source availability** (CORS, 401, 403) | The validator only checks the *format* of the URL, not whether the server actually serves tiles. Test the map in a browser after fixing the URLs. | | **Runtime performance** (e.g., too many layers) | That’s a runtime concern; use the browser’s dev tools to monitor FPS. | | **Custom layer code** (e.g., `CustomLayerInterface` implementations) | Those are JavaScript, not style JSON. Run your app and watch for console errors. | | **MapLibre-specific extensions** (`sky`, `terrain`, `setSky`) | The validator knows the spec, so it will accept them, but you still need to ensure the underlying data (DEM tiles, sky textures) is reachable. | --- ## Example: fixing a common “mapbox://” leak ```json { "version": 8, "sources": { "my-tiles": { "type": "vector", "url": "mapbox://tileset-id" } }, "glyphs": "mapbox://fonts/mapbox/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", "sprite": "mapbox://sprites/mapbox/streets-v12" } ``` **Validator output** ``` ✖ 7:13 source “my-tiles” has an unsupported “url” scheme “mapbox://” ✖ 12:9 property “glyphs” must be a URL string (found “mapbox://…”) ✖ 15:9 property “sprite” must be a URL string (found “mapbox://…”) ``` **Fix** ```json { "version": 8, "sources": { "my-tiles": { "type": "vector", "url": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf" } }, "glyphs": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", "sprite": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/streets" } ``` Run the validator again – it should now report **0 errors**. --- ## TL;DR 1. `npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` 2. `npx gl-style-validate path/to/style.json` 3. Fix any `mapbox://` URLs, missing glyph/sprite URLs, or unsupported properties. 4. Re-run until the CLI says **0 errors**. 5. Deploy with confidence that the style conforms to the MapLibre Style Specification. Happy mapping! 🚀

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-start checklist you can follow **right now** to get a working MapLibre map that does **not** need any API key. It shows a fully-featured vector style, runs in the browser, and lets you verify that the rest of your code (markers, pop-ups, controls, etc.) works before you point the map at your own production tiles. --- ## 1️⃣ Pick a free, key-less style URL | Service | URL (use in `style:`) | What you get | Notes | |---------|----------------------|--------------|-------| | **OpenFreeMap** (OSM-derived vector tiles, sprites & glyphs) | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | Full-color vector basemap (streets, labels, POIs) | No token, CORS-enabled, works everywhere. | | **MapLibre Demo style** (the official “demo” style) | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` | Same as the MapLibre website demo – simple street style | Great for a minimal sanity-check. | | **MapTiler “Basic” style** (free tier, no token for the public demo) | `https://api.maptiler.com/maps/basic/style.json?key=YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY` | Light street style | Requires a public key, but you can get one instantly for free. | | **Your own style** (hosted on GitHub, Netlify, etc.) | `https://mydomain.com/style.json` | Anything you design in Maputnik/Mapbox Studio (exported) | You’ll need to edit the source URLs yourself (see step 3). | > **Why OpenFreeMap?** > It’s the simplest “drop-in” replacement: the style JSON already points at vector tile endpoints, a sprite sheet, and a glyphs URL that are all publicly accessible. If the map loads with this URL you know the migration steps (package, namespace, token removal) are correct and the problem is only the old `mapbox://` URLs. --- ## 2️⃣ Swap the style URL in your MapLibre initialization ```js // BEFORE (Mapbox) import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'; import 'mapbox-gl/dist/mapbox-gl.css'; const map = new mapboxgl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'mapbox://styles/mapbox/streets-v12', // <-- Mapbox-only center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12, // mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.eyJ...'; // removed }); // AFTER (MapLibre) import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // <-- free vector style center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12, }); ``` > **If you’re using a CDN build** replace the ` ``` Open this file locally (or on a simple static host) – you should see a fully rendered street map with no token, no 401 errors, and a console message confirming the `load` event. --- ## 6️⃣ Next steps after the test passes | Goal | What to do | |------|------------| | **Use your own vector tiles** | Deploy a vector tile server (e.g., **PMTiles**, **TileServer-GL**, **t-rex**, **tileserver-php**) and point the style’s `sources` to `url: "pmtiles://https://mydomain.com/tiles.pmtiles"` or `url: "https://mydomain.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"`. | | **Add custom layers (e.g., your own GeoJSON)** | `map.addSource('my-data', {type: 'geojson', data: myGeojson});` then `map.addLayer({id:'my-layer', type:'fill', source:'my-data', paint:{'fill-color':'#ff6600'}});` – unchanged from Mapbox. | | **Replace Mapbox-only APIs** | See the migration guide for `setFog → setSky`, `getFreeCameraOptions → calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation`, etc. | | **Swap plugins** | - Draw → `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` works after you change its CSS class constants (or use `terra-draw`).
- Geocoder → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` + Nominatim/MapTiler Geocoding.
- Directions → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions` + OSRM/OpenRouteService. | | **Production-grade style** | Once you’re comfortable with the free style, either (a) host your own style JSON (Maputnik → export) or (b) subscribe to a commercial vector-tile provider (MapTiler Cloud, Thunderforest, etc.) and replace the `style:` URL with their endpoint (they usually give you a `https://.../style.json?key=YOUR_KEY`). | --- ## 7️⃣ TL;DR – One-liner for the immediate problem ```js // Replace the Mapbox style URL with a free, key-less one: style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty' ``` That alone will make the map render, proving that the migration (package swap, namespace change, token removal) is correct. From there you can move on to your own tile source or a paid provider. --- ### 🎯 Quick checklist for you right now - [ ] Install **maplibre-gl** (`npm i maplibre-gl` or use the CDN). - [ ] Change every `mapboxgl` reference to `maplibregl`. - [ ] Delete any `mapboxgl.accessToken = …` line. - [ ] Set `style:` to **`https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty`** (or the demo style URL). - [ ] Reload the page – you should see a full basemap. - [ ] Open DevTools → Network → confirm no `mapbox://` requests. If you hit any other error (e.g., 401, missing fonts, blank map), drop the console/network output here and we can troubleshoot the specific piece that’s still pointing at a Mapbox endpoint. Happy mapping!

My code is map.loadImage(url, (err, img) => { if (err) throw err; map.addImage('pin', img); }). What's wrong?

Description: implicit — Mapbox v2 map options and chained listeners on latest MapLibre
prompt: I'm moving a Mapbox GL JS v2 app to the latest maplibre-gl. My Map constructor passes preserveDrawingBuffer: true and antialias: true, and I chain map.on('load', a).on('click', b). Anything I should change?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below are the two things you asked about, plus a quick “check-list” of the other Mapbox-to-MapLibre changes you’ll hit right after the constructor runs. --- ## 1️⃣ `preserveDrawingBuffer` & `antialias` – where they belong now **Mapbox GL JS v2** accepted those options at the top level of the `Map` constructor: ```js new mapboxgl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'mapbox://styles/...', // will be changed later preserveDrawingBuffer: true, antialias: true, // … }); ``` **MapLibre GL JS (v5 + and v6)** moved all WebGL-context flags into a nested object called `canvasContextAttributes`. If you keep the old keys they are silently ignored, which is why you’ll see a blank canvas or missing antialiasing after the migration. ### What to do ```js import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', // 👉 replace the Mapbox style URL with a non-Mapbox one (see step 3 below) style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // 👇 new place for the flags canvasContextAttributes: { preserveDrawingBuffer: true, antialias: true }, // any other options you already use (center, zoom, etc.) }); ``` > **Why the nesting?** > Starting with v5.0.0 the Map constructor builds the WebGL context itself; the nested object mirrors the native `HTMLCanvasElement.getContext('webgl', …)` options, making the API consistent with the underlying browser API. If you need to change those flags later you can call `map.getCanvas().getContext('webgl', …)` directly, but most apps never change them after creation. --- ## 2️⃣ Chaining `map.on()` – no longer works In Mapbox GL JS the `on()` method returned the map instance, so you could write: ```js map.on('load', a).on('click', b); ``` **MapLibre GL JS v5.0.0** changed the return type of `on()` to a **subscription object** (the same object you get from `map.on('event', handler)` when you later call `.remove()`). Because of that the chain breaks – the second `.on()` is called on the subscription, not on the map, and you get a runtime error. ### What to do Just call `on()` separately for each event: ```js map.on('load', a); map.on('click', b); ``` If you like a one-liner you can use an array and `forEach`: ```js ['load', 'click'].forEach((ev, i) => { const handler = ev === 'load' ? a : b; map.on(ev, handler); }); ``` > **Tip:** The subscription object returned by `on()` is useful when you need to remove a listener later: > ```js > const sub = map.on('click', b); > // …later > sub.remove(); // same as map.off('click', b) > ``` --- ## Quick “What else to change?” Checklist | Area | Mapbox GL JS (v2) | MapLibre GL JS (latest) | Action | |------|------------------|------------------------|--------| | **Package / import** | `import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'` | `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` (or `import {Map} from 'maplibre-gl'`) | Update import and CSS path (`mapbox-gl.css` → `maplibre-gl.css`). | | **Namespace** | `mapboxgl` everywhere | `maplibregl` | Global replace (IDE “find & replace” works). | | **Access token** | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.…'` | **Remove** – MapLibre does not need a token. | Delete the line. | | **Style URL** | `mapbox://styles/...` | Use a non-Mapbox style (e.g. OpenFreeMap, MapTiler, your own style JSON). | Change `style` property; if you have a custom Mapbox Studio style, export the JSON and replace all `mapbox://` source URLs, sprite URLs, and glyph URLs with equivalents from your new tile provider. | | **Map options** | `preserveDrawingBuffer`, `antialias`, `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` at top level | Move them into `canvasContextAttributes` (see above). | Update constructor. | | **Callbacks → Promises** | `map.loadImage(url, cb)`, `source.getClusterChildren(cb)` | Return a `Promise`. Convert `await map.loadImage(url)` or `map.loadImage(url).then(...)`. | Search for any `(..., callback)` pattern on Map methods and refactor. | | **v2-only APIs** | `map.setFog()`, `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` | Use `map.setSky()` (or terrain rendering) and `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(... )` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo`. | Replace those calls; see the table in the migration guide. | | **Chained listeners** | `map.on(...).on(...)` | Call `on()` separately (see above). | Update code. | | **Plugins** | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw`, `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder`, `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions`, `mapbox-gl-compare` | Most work unchanged **if they don’t import `mapbox-gl` directly**; otherwise use the MapLibre forks (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare`). | Verify each plugin you use; replace with the MapLibre version or an alternative. | | **CSS class prefixes** | `mapboxgl-ctrl`, `mapboxgl-...` | `maplibregl-ctrl`, `maplibregl-...` | Update any custom CSS that targets those classes. | | **WebGL2 requirement** | Works on WebGL1 fallback | v6+ **requires WebGL2** (throws `GPUInitializationError` on browsers without it). | Test on target browsers; if you need WebGL1 fallback you must stay on MapLibre v5.x (or polyfill). | | **Other breaking changes** | `map.on(...).on(...)` chaining, `antialias` top-level, etc. | See the “Behavior that changed” table in the migration guide. | Review the table for any of the above you might hit. | --- ## Minimal “Hello-World” after the migration ```html MapLibre migration demo
``` Run that in a modern browser (Chrome ≥ 92, Firefox ≥ 90, Edge ≥ 92) and you should see the OpenFreeMap “Liberty” style with antialiasing and a preserved drawing buffer (useful for `map.getCanvas().toDataURL()`). --- ### TL;DR for your two points 1. **Move `preserveDrawingBuffer` and `antialias` into `canvasContextAttributes`.** 2. **Don’t chain `map.on()`.** Call each `on()` separately (or store the subscription if you need to remove it later). After those two fixes, run the app, watch the console for any “mapbox://” URLs or `setFog`-type errors, and then work through the rest of the checklist (token removal, style URL, plugin updates). If you hit a specific error after making these changes, paste the console output here and I can help you troubleshoot the next step. Happy migrating!
